prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity 16:10 desktop web app UI comp
Primary request: Design a serious EPL decision-support workspace called “Pick Optimizer” in the visual direction “Graphite Model Console”. This is a real product interface, not a poster, not concept art, and explicitly not a betting app.
Canvas and framing: single straight-on 16:10 desktop application screen, edge-to-edge persistent graphite workspace, no browser chrome, no device frame, no perspective. Dense but calm professional data UI with a slim left navigation rail, slim top season/status bar, large center candidate comparison table, expanded right-side future-delta inspector, and a compact remaining-season timeline along the bottom.
Content and exact text: season “2026–27”; “Matchweek 1”; app label “PICK OPTIMIZER”; status “MODEL READY”; navigation labels “OPTIMIZE”, “SEASON”, “RULES”, “AUDIT”. Main heading “Ranked candidates”. Show exactly three fixture rows ranked 01–03: “Arsenal vs Coventry”, “Man City vs Bournemouth”, “Liverpool vs Nott’m Forest”. Table columns “WIN PROB.”, “EXPECTED PTS”, “SEASON COST”, “FUTURE WEEK”. Use plausible modeling values without sportsbook formatting: Arsenal “72%”, “3.00”, “£6.4m”, “MW 8”; Man City “69%”, “2.91”, “£7.1m”, “MW 5”; Liverpool “66%”, “2.78”, “£5.9m”, “MW 12”. Arsenal row is selected with restrained teal outline/tint, not bright green. Primary button text “Commit Arsenal”.
Right panel exact text: “FUTURE DELTA”, “Arsenal selected”, “Season impact”, “+0.18 expected pts”, “Affected week”, “MW 8 · Arsenal vs Brentford”, “Opportunity cost”, “LOW”, and a small stepped line plot labeled “BASELINE” and “WITH PICK”.
Bottom strip exact text: “REMAINING SEASON”; a compact horizontal Matchweek timeline from “MW 1” through “MW 38” with only sparse labeled checkpoints MW 1, MW 5, MW 8, MW 12, MW 20, MW 30, MW 38; teal marker for the current selection impact at MW 8, amber marker for the next constraint at MW 12.
Style/medium: ultra-polished realistic product UI screenshot, serious football analytics and observability/modeling console, compact sans-serif typography with uppercase micro-labels and monospaced tabular figures. Strong information hierarchy at desktop density. Hairline seams, one subtle step of elevation only, squared corners with a restrained 4–6px radius, fine grid alignment, crisp vector-like icons and charts.
Color palette: background #111417, primary text #E9EDF0, restrained teal #6FA8A0 for active selection, amber #D5A65A for warnings/constraints, slate #59636B for secondary labels and separators. Near-black graphite panels, off-white text.
Composition details: left nav about 64px wide with simple line icons; top status bar about 52px tall; center area gets most width; right future panel about 30% of content width and visibly expanded because Arsenal is selected. Comparison behaves like one integrated data surface rather than separate cards. The bottom timeline spans center and right content. Include compact confidence bars and a minimal probability tick ruler where useful, keeping all data readable.
Lighting/mood: flat digital interface rendering, sober, precise, calm, credible, premium engineering tool.
Constraints: render all requested interface text verbatim and legibly; show all three ranked candidate fixtures; prominent but compact “Commit Arsenal” action; make the product clearly about choosing an EPL survivor/pick strategy across a season; use only one subtle layer of elevation; maintain generous enough spacing for legibility despite compact density.
Avoid: sportsbook odds, betting slips, casino styling, red/green win-loss states, neon, gradients, glassmorphism, glowing effects, shadows beyond one subtle elevation, card collage, giant title, giant KPI numbers, marketing hero layout, football photography, club crests, logos, stadium imagery, decorative trophies, invented claims, fake testimonials, clutter, excessive rounded cards, mobile UI, poster composition, watermarks.
